subject: Issues adding forcing function to SIR-style DE model

messages.author: 08d7d872077e52b9
messages.subject: Issues adding forcing function to SIR-style DE model
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to estimate parameters for an SIRB (susceptible-infected-recovered-bacteria) model for cholera transmission in India. I had managed to make a simplified version work using simulated dummy data. I am now trying to introduce a forcing function (in this case, temperature) to my differential equations, and am using the R function approxfun() to do this. While the DE function itself is working with the forcing function, the NIMBLE model now gives me the following warnings, an then an error:

warning: value of deterministic node z[1:999, 1:4]: value is NA or NaN even after trying to calculate.
warning: value of stochastic node y[999]: value is NA or NaN even after trying to simulate.
warning: problem initializing stochastic node y[999]: logProb is NA or NaN.
|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
|Warning: AF slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions in at least one dimension.

This is a stand-alone version of my code to demonstrate the issue:
library(deSolve)
library(nimble)
library(dplyr)

######################################## FUNCTIONS ##############################################
#Force of infection
f <- function(B){
  lambda <- B/(B + kappa)
  return(lambda)
}

#SIRB equations for creating simulated data
SIRB_equations <- function(time, variables, parms) {
  with(as.list(c(parms, variables)), {
    temp_signal <- temp_fun(time)
    dS <- mu*(H-S)  -  f(B)*S  +  rho*R
    dI <- nu*f(B)*S  -  (mu+alpha+eta)*I
    dR <- (1-nu)*f(B)*S  +  eta*I  -  (rho+mu)*R
    dB <- epsilon*I  -  (mu_B*B) / (temp_signal ^ Lambda)
    res <- c(dS, dI, dR, dB)
    list(res)
  })
}

#Make sure we don't get any negative values when simulating data
positive <- function(x){
  if (x < 0){y <- 0}
  else{y <- x}
  return(y)
}

#SIRB equations for NIMBLE
SIRB_equations_nimble <- function(t=0:999, z, theta){
  temp_signal <- temp_fun(t)
  H <- 10000 #Population size
  kappa <- 0.9 * 10**6 #Half saturation constant
  nu <- 0.8 #Proportion of symptomatic infections
  rho <- 0.4 #Rate of immunity loss
  mu <- 0.001 #Birth/death rate
  alpha <- 0.01 #Case fatality ratio
  eta <- 0.2 #Recovery rate
  S <- z[1]
  I <- z[2]
  R <- z[3]
  B <- z[4]
  epsilon <- theta[1]
  mu_B <- theta[2]
  dS <- mu*(H-S)  -  f(B)*S  +  rho*R
  dI <- nu*f(B)*S  -  (mu+alpha+eta)*I
  dR <- (1-nu)*f(B)*S  +  eta*I  -  (rho+mu)*R
  dB <- epsilon*I  -  (mu_B*B) / (temp_signal ^ Lambda)
  return(list(c(dS, dI, dR, dB)))
}


ODEfun <- function(z_init,theta){
  as.matrix(ode(y = z_init, times = 0:999, func=SIRB_equations_nimble, parms = theta))[-1,-1]
}

nimODE <- nimbleRcall(function(z_init = double(1), theta = double(1)){}, Rfun = 'ODEfun',
                      returnType = double(2))


##################################### SET UP DUMMY DATA ############################################


#Estimated Parameters
H <- 10000 #Population size
kappa <- 0.9 * 10**6 #Half saturation constant
nu <- 0.8 #Proportion of symptomatic infections
rho <- 0.4 #Rate of immunity loss
mu <- 0.001 #Birth/death rate
alpha <- 0.01 #Case fatality ratio
eta <- 0.2 #Recovery rate
Lambda <- 0.1 #Temp factor

#Parameters which will be estimated
theta <- c(epsilon = 10, mu_B = 0.33)

#Number of unknown parameters in this model
num_params <- 2

#Initial Conditions
I0 <- 10
B0 <- 10000
R0 <- 0
S0 <- H - I0 - R0

#Initial values
z_init <- c(S = S0, I = I0, R = R0, B = B0)

#Time series
num_days = 1000
M <- num_days - 1
ts <- seq(0,M)

#Simulated temperature data (forcing function)
temp_sim <- 7*sin((ts)*(6.282/365)) + 27 + rnorm(length(ts),0,1)
temp_fun <- approxfun(ts,temp_sim)

Analyse DEs
SIRB_values <- as.matrix(ode(y = z_init, times = ts, SIRB_equations, parms = theta))
df <- data.frame(SIRB_values)

#Create some noise
sigma = 100
noise <- replicate(4, rnorm(dim(SIRB_values)[1], 0, sd = sigma))

noisy_SIRB <- SIRB_values[,2:5] + noise
pos_noisy<- pmax(noisy_SIRB,0)
colnames(pos_noisy) <- c("S_noise", "I_noise", "R_noise", "B_noise")
df <- data.frame(cbind(SIRB_values, pos_noisy))

############################################### NIMBLE MODEL ##########################################
infection_data <- unlist(df[-c(1),]["I_noise"])
num_chains = 4


Model <- nimbleCode({
  for(i in 1:n){
    y[i] ~ dnorm(z[i,2],tau)
  }
  z[1:n,1:4] <- nimODE(z_init=z_init[1:4],theta=theta[1:2])
  ## Priors
  tau <- 1/(sigma*sigma) #NIMBLE takes precision (tau) as input rather than variance
  sigma ~ T(dnorm(0,1),0,) #T() means 'truncated'
  theta[1] ~ T(dnorm(0,sd = 5),0,) #epsilon = 10
  theta[2] ~ T(dnorm(0,sd = 5),0,) #mu_B = 0.33    
})
Consts <- list(n = M)
nimbleData <- list(y=infection_data,z_init = z_init)
inits <- list( theta=c(1,1),sigma=0.1)
nimbleModel <- nimbleModel(code=Model, name='nimbleModel', constants = Consts, data = nimbleData, inits = inits)
MCMCconfig <- configureMCMC(nimbleModel,monitors=c("theta","sigma"))
MCMCconfig$removeSamplers("theta")
MCMCconfig$addSampler(target="theta",type='AF_slice')
modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(MCMCconfig)
compiled_model <- compileNimble(nimbleModel, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
compiled_model_MCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = nimbleModel, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

results <- runMCMC(compiled_model_MCMC, niter = 5000, nburnin = 2000, nchains = num_chains, thin=10,
                   inits=inits, progressBar = T, samplesAsCodaMCMC = T)

I'm relatively new to Nimble and I'm not quite sure where to go from here. Any advice would be much appreciated!

Thank you!
Debbie

Hi Debbie

The problem comes from NAs in node z.  

> tail(nimbleModel$z, n=3)

[999,]       NA           NA           NA           NA

> SIRB_values <- as.matrix(ode(y = z_init, times = ts, SIRB_equations, parms = theta))

> tail(SIRB_values, n=3)

 [998,]  997 5770.219 332.2924 210.2046 13725.41

[1000,]  999       NA       NA       NA       NA

So to dig a bit deeper, I tinkered with one of your functions...

SIRB_equations_nimble <- function(t, z, theta){
  temp_signal <- temp_fun(t)
  H           <- 10000       # Population size
  kappa       <- 0.9 * 10**6 # Half saturation constant
  nu          <- 0.8         # Proportion of symptomatic infections
  rho         <- 0.4         # Rate of immunity loss

alpha       <- 0.01        # Case fatality ratio
  eta         <- 0.2         # Recovery rate

S           <- z[1]
  I           <- z[2]
  R           <- z[3]
  B           <- z[4]
  epsilon     <- theta[1]
  mu_B        <- theta[2]
dS          <- mu*(H-S) + rho*R        - f(B)*S

dI          <- nu*f(B)*S               - (mu+alpha+eta)*I
  dR          <- (1-nu)*f(B)*S  +  eta*I - (rho+mu)*R
  dB          <- epsilon*I               - (mu_B*B) / (temp_signal ^ Lambda)

returnList  <- list(c(dS=dS, dI=dI, dR=dR, dB=dB))
  printList   <- list(c( S=S,   I=I,   R=R,   B=B))
  print(list(printList, returnList, temp_fun(t)))
  return(returnList)
}

Now if I try to build the nimble model it spits out the following (truncated)  blurb  

[[1]]
[[1]][[1]]
         S.S          I.I          R.R          B.B
9.997533e+03 4.161282e-83 2.191714e-19 7.618154e-83


[[2]]
[[2]][[1]]
         dS.S          dI.B          dR.B          dB.I
 2.467288e-03 -8.103303e-84 -8.788772e-20 -1.487038e-83


[[3]]
[1] 19.9207

[[1]]
[[1]][[1]]
         S.S          I.I          R.R          B.B
9.997533e+03 4.161282e-83 4.116627e-83 2.191714e-19


[[2]]
[[2]][[1]]
         dS.S          dI.B          dR.B          dB.I
 2.467288e-03  1.947709e-21  4.869273e-22 -1.625000e-19


[[3]]
[1] 19.9207

[[1]]
[[1]][[1]]
         S.S          I.I          R.R          B.B
9.997535e+03 3.416524e-83 3.379927e-83 6.256053e-83


[[2]]
[[2]][[1]]
         dS.S          dI.B          dR.B          dB.I
 2.464822e-03 -6.652910e-84 -6.581469e-84            NA


[[3]]
[1] NA

Checking model sizes and dimensions
  [Note] This model is not fully initialized. This is not an error.
         To see which variables are not initialized, use model$initializeInfo().
         For more information on model initialization, see help(modelInitialization).

This is telling me that temp_fun(t) is generating an NA. Indeed...

> temp_fun(999)
[1] 19.93928
> temp_fun(1000)
[1] NA

So I adjusted your script (i.e. added the Nigel Tufnel hack) so that temp_fun(1000)no longer returns NA (attached). 

Now that there are no longer NAs in z your nimble model can return a finite logProb and you can start doing some MCMC. 

Hope that helps
David

parts:
One further comment

I strongly suggest looking into using C (and not R) for providing gradients to ode. The speed up will be considerable, and your effective sample size from MCMC will go up considerably. Well worth the investment of time to set it up!   There are some examples of how to do that here
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/deSolve/vignettes/compiledCode.pdf

Cheers

David

  with(as.list(c(parms, variables)), {
    temp_signal <- temp_fun(time)
    dS <- mu*(H-S)  -  f(B)*S  +  rho*R
    dI <- nu*f(B)*S  -  (mu+alpha+eta)*I
    dR <- (1-nu)*f(B)*S  +  eta*I  -  (rho+mu)*R
    dB <- epsilon*I  -  (mu_B*B) / (temp_signal ^ Lambda)
    res <- c(dS, dI, dR, dB)
    list(res)
  })
}

#Make sure we don't get any negative values when simulating data
positive <- function(x){
  if (x < 0){y <- 0}
  else{y <- x}
  return(y)
}

#SIRB equations for NIMBLE
SIRB_equations_nimble <- function(t=0:999, z, theta){
  temp_signal <- temp_fun(t)
  H <- 10000 #Population size
  kappa <- 0.9 * 10**6 #Half saturation constant
  nu <- 0.8 #Proportion of symptomatic infections
  rho <- 0.4 #Rate of immunity loss
  mu <- 0.001 #Birth/death rate
  alpha <- 0.01 #Case fatality ratio
  eta <- 0.2 #Recovery rate
  S <- z[1]
  I <- z[2]
  R <- z[3]
  B <- z[4]
  epsilon <- theta[1]
  mu_B <- theta[2]
  dS <- mu*(H-S)  -  f(B)*S  +  rho*R
  dI <- nu*f(B)*S  -  (mu+alpha+eta)*I
  dR <- (1-nu)*f(B)*S  +  eta*I  -  (rho+mu)*R
  dB <- epsilon*I  -  (mu_B*B) / (temp_signal ^ Lambda)
  return(list(c(dS, dI, dR, dB)))
}


ODEfun <- function(z_init,theta){
  as.matrix(ode(y = z_init, times = 0:999, func=SIRB_equations_nimble, parms = theta))[-1,-1]
}
